points.text: Yunus (a.s) was from the descendants of Ibraheem (a.s). He was sent as a Rasool to city of Nineveh which is modern day Mosul, in northern Iraq. It was a populous city with over a hundred thousand people.

While Yunus called his people to turn to Allah and shun idol worship, the people rejected him and made fun of him. After calling his people for long, he got disheartened and gave up on his people. He left the city in anger and without Allah’s permission and he wanted to find another community who would accept him and enter the fold of Islam.

When he had left, the skies of Nineveh turned red and it was clear that the wrath of Allah was about to fall upon the entire city. Seeing this, all the men, women and children gathered at the mountain tops. They remembered Yunus’s warnings of Allah’s punishment and feared that they will have the same punishment as the people of Ad, Thamud and people of Nuh.

All the people fell on their knees, and with their hands stretched out, they began to beg for Allah’s forgiveness and mercy. Seeing this sincere act of repentance, Allah forgave the people and lifted the scourge that was to fall upon them. The people thanked Allah and prayed for the safe return of Yunus (a.s) so that he can guide them to the path of Allah.

Meanwhile, Yunus had boarded a small passenger ship with the intention of traveling far away from his people. One night, a storm raged upon the ocean wherein the crew and passengers began to fear for their lives as the sea water began flooding into the decks, slowly sinking the ship.

As the storm raged on, the captain of the ship ordered that all the luggage be thrown out of the ship. The boat continued to sink as it was still too heavy. The captain was left with no choice but to sacrifice one man if he wished to save the lives of his crew and passengers. As it was common practice among men during those times, the Captain decided to draw lots to choose the passengers to be sacrificed.
The lots were cast and Yunus’s name came up. The men on the boat knew that Yunus was a young, righteous, honest and blessed man; so they refused to thrown him out and agreed to draw lots again.

So they drew lots again and Yunus’s name came up. They refused to accept and drew lots for a third time. Also, the third time Yunus’s name came up. Yunus knew that this was the verdict of Allah for he had left his people without Allah’s consent. So, Yunus was thrown into the sea. Then as per Allah’s command a whale swallowed him just as he hit the waters.

Yunus, who was unconscious woke up to find himself in the belly of the whale. He prostrated to Allah where no man has ever prostrated before, and pleaded for Allah’s forgiveness with a dua which is beautifully captured in Surah Al-Anbiya as below.

Allah accepted his repentance and commanded the whale to spit out Yunus at the nearest shore. Allah caused a tree to grow on the shore where Yunus was lying down, and this gave him food and shelter until he recovered fully and then got back to his people in Nineveh. The entire population of Nineveh accepted Islam upon the arrival of Yunus, and Yunus prostrated to his Rabb and thanked Allah for all His blessings. This story is beautifully captured in few ayahs of the Quran as below: (Above source from At-Tabari)

verses.text: Yunus (a.s) (Jonah) was surely one of the Rasools. He ran away to the laden ship (without the permission of his Rabb). When he took part in the casting of lots, he lost and was thrown in to the sea. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 5)
A whale swallowed him, for he had become blameworthy. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 5)
Had he not repented and became of those who glorify Allah, he would have certainly remained inside its belly till the Day of Resurrection. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 5)
Then Allah cast him upon a desolate shore in a state of serious illness and caused a gourd plant to grow over him. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 5)
Allah sent him to a nation of one hundred thousand people or more. They believed in him, so Allah permitted them to enjoy their life for a while. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 5)
Allah blessed Dhun-Nun (or Yunus a.s, also known as Jonah). (Surah Al-Anbiya: Section 6)
When he departed in anger, thinking Allah would not take him to task for this. (He was swallowed by the whale) and he prayed from the depths of darkness: (Surah Al-Anbiya: Section 6)
“There is none worthy of worship but You, glory be to You! Indeed, I was the one who committed wrong”. Allah accepted his prayer and delivered him from distress. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 6)
The only town, which upon seeing the scourge, believed and their belief profited them, were the people of Yunus. (Surah Yunus : Section 10)
When they believed, Allah removed from them the disgraceful scourge (which was to come) and allowed them to enjoy their worldly life for a while. (Surah Yunus : Section 10)
